sentences.text: The application stands disposed of.

1. This is a petition under Article 227 of the Constitution of India read with Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of FIR No.334/2017, under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Keshav Puram, Delhi, and all proceedings emanating therefrom.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/12/2023 at 23:27:45 2.
Issue notice.
Learned APP appears on advance notice, and accepts notice.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 28.04.2015 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies and they lived together as husband and wife with each other.
One female child was born out of the said wedlock on 06.06.2016.
Thereafter, the disputes and differences arose between them and they started living separately since 06.08.2016.
On 30.05.2017, the respondent No.2 got the above said FIR registered against the petitioners.

sentences.text: Counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, the parties have settled the matter amicably in terms of the MOU dated 14.09.2023.
Copy of the said settlement is placed on record.

Accordingly, the petition under Section 13B(2) of the HMA was allowed and the marriage of the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 was dissolved vide decree of divorce dated 03.11.2023 passed by the learned Principal Judge, Family Courts, Rohini, Delhi.

entities.text: Principal Judge, Family Courts, Rohini, Delhi
entities.label: JUDGE

sentences.text: The copy of the decree of divorce is already on record.
5. Petitioners and respondent no.2 are present in Court today and they have been identified by the IO.
I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.
Respondent No.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioners.
She further submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily, without any force, pressure or coercion.
As per settlement, today, a demand draft of Rs. 20,00,000/- (bearing no. 803933 dated 16.11.2023 drawn on IDFC First Bank) has been handed over to respondent no.2.
Respondent No.2 submits This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/12/2023 at 23:27:45 that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
6. Learned APP for the State submits that in view of the settlement, the State has no objection if the FIR in question be quashed.
7. Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.

Consequentially, this petition is allowed and FIR No.334/2017,
under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Keshav Puram, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom shall stand quashed.

However, the rights of the child born from the wedlock of petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 are left open to be adjudicated by him/her as and when he/she attains majority as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ganesh vs.
Sudhirkumar Shrivastava & Ors, decided on 22.04.2019 in Civil Appeal Nos.4031-4032 of 2019.
8. The present petition stands disposed of accordingly.
RAJNISH BHATNAGAR, J DECEMBER 18, 2023/
